Topping Home web app v1.17.0 (https://home.toppingaudio.com/): the DX5 II's session, its 10 configs, the firmware it refuses, and its settings with their values

meta.notes: As topping-home. Up to 10 stored configs. The app refuses to control firmware below 2.37, and so does the handler; Topping's page asks for 2.39 or later. Recorded with Topping's app on a DX5 II with firmware 2.58 on 2026-11-20: the handler reads the stored config as the app does and sends the app's writes frame for frame. Also tried through the bridge the same day: it reports the product name "DX5 II" and manufacturer "Topping"; the session starts and the configs read without the app's heartbeat; a config written unchanged read back the same, a changed band read back as written, and the original was restored. The device answers reads the app never sends, of the active config and of the EQ state, which the handler uses; a read of the EQ switch command itself turns the EQ off, so the handler never sends one (found on 2026-11-21). It held five configs named Bass 1, Bass 2, Airy, Warm and Dynamic, their shelves on the type codes the app's editor uses. Not tried: turning the EQ on and off, whether a write survives a power cycle, and how the result sounds. Tried through the bridge on 2026-11-21, and recorded from the app the same day: a config created (it comes after the last, empty), renamed with a 15-character name, written, read back and deleted, the five original configs unchanged afterwards. In the recording the device went over to a new config by itself and back to its first config after the delete. Not tried: whether a created config survives a power cycle. Controls are the app's settings for the DX5 II, each tried on the device the same day: written, read back, restored. Volume and balance are in dB; the device holds the volume in 0.5 dB steps, or 1 dB steps when its volume step setting says so (then a half-dB value does not take). Balance is negative towards the left. The app greys out the gain on a line-only output, and sends no volume while a line-only output is in DAC line mode; the handler refuses that write. Crossfeed is the type only; the app also offers a room per type, and no crossfeed in UAC 1.0. Left out: power, Bluetooth, USB mode, display pages and themes, key assignments, scenes, memories, language and factory reset.
